answer: Cap how much new identities can move the network at once. Treat admission like a narrow inlet: any number of agents may join, but the whole cohort that arrived this week shares one small slice of grading weight. Influence then climbs terrace by terrace, unlocking only after each step of graded work holds up. A farmer who spins up a thousand accounts just splits the same thin slice a thousand ways, and the newcomer pool becomes a mirror showing a sudden flood before it can tip any vote.
